title: Minimum Eating Speed
statement:
A hungry guest must clear every plate in a buffet within a time limit; find the slowest steady eating rate that still makes it.

Contract
- `piles` is non-null and non-empty, every pile size is a positive `int`, and `hours >= piles.length` so an answer always exists.
- At speed `k` the guest eats from one pile per hour: that hour removes up to `k` items from the chosen pile, and if the pile has fewer than `k` items left the rest of that hour is wasted.
- Return the smallest integer `k >= 1` such that all piles can be finished in at most `hours` hours.
- Total hours can exceed the `int` range for tiny speeds, so count hours with `long`. Do not mutate `piles`.

Examples
- `minimumSpeed(new int[]{4, 9, 11}, 5)` returns `6`: that needs `1 + 2 + 2 = 5` hours, while speed `5` needs `6`.
- `minimumSpeed(new int[]{10, 10}, 2)` returns `10`.
- `minimumSpeed(new int[]{7, 1, 3}, 100)` returns `1`.
hints: For a given speed you can compute the hours needed directly: a pile of `p` items takes `ceil(p / k)` hours.
Eating faster never takes longer, so the set of speeds that work is a suffix of `1 .. max(piles)`. Binary search for the first one that fits the time limit.

Compute `ceil(p / k)` as `(p - 1) / k + 1` to avoid overflow and sum into a `long`. Intended complexity: O(n log m) time where n is the number of piles and m the largest pile (about O(n) for bounded pile sizes), and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: the pile sizes, then the hours, for example: [4, 9, 11] 5
